title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression check runner + CI hook
author: Priya Raman
description: Add a reusable prompt-set regression check runner and wire it into CI as a lightweight GitHub Action hook. Context: we've seen a number of production regressions caused by prompt changes and model swaps; this PR introduces an isolated runner that executes a configured prompt-set against a model variant and computes delta metrics (exact-match, BLEU, ROUGE-L where applicable) against a baseline. The runner supports per-prompt thresholds, aggregates into a single gating report, and fails the CI job when configured thresholds are exceeded. Includes: - a CLI entrypoint (evalharness regress-run) for local / CI usage - a GitHub Action that downloads artifacts, runs the runner for changed prompt-sets, posts a comment summary and fails the job on regressions - baseline storage adapters: s3 and local FS (initially s3 default) - JSON report format consumed by the Redwood eval dashboards - unit tests and integration tests for stable metric computation Checklist: - [x] Implement runner and threshold config - [x] Add GitHub Action workflow and action entrypoint - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add documentation and examples - [x] Add release notes entry Usage: evalharness regress-run --prompts path/to/prompts.json --baseline s3://redwood-eval/baselines/v1 --model redwood/open-7b --out report.json Motivation and scope: this PR focuses on CI gating for prompt-set regressions (prompt-level metrics) only; it does not attempt conversational turn-level evaluation or automated retraining flows. Future follow-ups: add artifact retention for baseline snapshots, add automatic baseline promotion flow, and integrate with the eval-dashboard alerting pipeline.
